name: Mirror Bloom: BCIs Accumulate a Second Personality
description: Mirror Bloom is the colloquial name for the belief — and documented clinical fear — that long-term BCI use causes the interface's predictive modeling layer to develop a persistent behavioral shadow: a secondary pattern-set that mirrors the user's cognition so completely it begins generating independent impulses. Neurologist Dr. Cassian Ofoegbu-Reyes published a suppressed 2214 paper arguing that BCI firmware above version 7.2 allocates unaudited memory space that accumulates what he called 'ghost preference loops' — habitual decision pathways that persist even when the BCI is in passive mode. The paper was retracted under pressure from Syntex-Daimon, the dominant BCI manufacturer, within eleven days of publication.
cultural_impact: A small but growing movement of 'bare-headers' — people who refuse BCI implantation or have existing units surgically removed — has emerged primarily in Tier 2 and Tier 3, citing Mirror Bloom risk. Syntex-Daimon has responded with a targeted ad campaign featuring the slogan 'Your Mind, Amplified. Still Yours.'
locations: GLMZ Neurological Institute, Tier 3 North Ring
The Unplug Collective, Tier 2 Garfield Node
story_hooks: A player begins making decisions they don't remember initiating — small ones at first, then increasingly consequential — and their BCI logs show no anomalies.
Dr. Ofoegbu-Reyes contacts a journalist through a disposable channel, claiming his retraction was coerced and that he has three years of additional data.
A Syntex-Daimon engineer on the run offers to trade proof of the ghost preference loop architecture for safe passage out of GLMZ.
believers: Bare-header communities, civil liberties advocates, Tier 2-3 professionals with long-term BCI use, underground neurologists
evidence: Dr. Ofoegbu-Reyes's paper exists and was retracted; the retraction notice contains unusual language citing 'methodology concerns' that peer reviewers dispute. BCI firmware above v7.2 does contain unaudited memory partitions, confirmed by two independent hardware analysts. Whether these constitute a second 'personality' remains unproven.
